New Westminster real estate market stats for September 2026: benchmark prices and trends
New Westminster houses by price band, September 2026

9 houses sold in September against 164 listed. The price band with the most sales was $1,250,001 to $1,500,000, with 7 sold (78% of the month). Among bands with at least ten homes listed, the highest sales ratio was $1,250,001 to $1,500,000 at 21%.

faq.q: How did New Westminster sell in September 2026?
faq.a: City-wide: 164 detached listings with only 9 sold at a $1,365,000 median, and 444 Condos & Townhomes listings with 67 sold at a $560,000 median — the attached median's lowest month in the September 2025 – September 2026 period; the highest published ratios were GlenBrooke North and The Heights detached, joint at 12%, and the Quay attached at 27% on 16 sales (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Is Queensborough part of New Westminster?
faq.a: Yes — Queensborough is a New Westminster board sub-area and city neighbourhood across the Fraser River from the mainland city; it carried the city's largest detached shelf in September 2026 (41 listings, 1 sale, 2%) and its own schools confirmed in the Ministry file, Queen Elizabeth Elementary (921 Salter St) and Queensborough Middle School (833 Salter St) (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report) (~/workspace/area-research-2026-11/education/work/bc_k12_schools.csv, read 2026-11-01).

faq.q: How many units can a New Westminster house lot hold?
faq.a: Since June 2026, OCP and Zoning Bylaw amendments permit up to six units of infill housing — suites, laneway and carriage houses, triplex, quadplex and other multiplex forms — on single detached and duplex properties across most of the city, under RGO-A (up to four units) and RGO-B (up to six units) zoning, without a site-specific rezoning.

faq.q: When are property taxes due in New Westminster?
faq.a: For 2026, City of New Westminster property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to current taxes remaining (including unclaimed Home Owner Grants) on July 3, 2026, and a second 5% penalty applies to any unpaid balance on September 3, 2026.
